newsitem.title: UK: Stg weakness lifts shares in big UK exporters.
newsitem.headline: Stg weakness lifts shares in big UK exporters.

text.p: Sterling's retreat on Wednesday helped shares in companies whose profits have been damaged by the strong pound, sector analysts and strategists said.
"The market may be beginning to feel that the worst is behind them on currencies," said Charterhouse head of research, Richard Jeffrey.

Sterling extended its slide under 3.02 marks and below $1.60 to trade four pfennigs and three cents below session highs amid growing belief that this week's monetary meeting might leave British interest rates unchanged at 6.75 percent.
The leading FTSE 100 index surged to record highs on robust company profits news and was helped by sterling's retreat.
GKN Plc shares rose 73-1/2p after releasing better-than-expected first-half figures and currency factors, traders said.
Other big overseas earners also benefited from sterling's demise. ICI Plc advanced 22p to 1,050p, TI Group Plc 26-1/2p to 581p and Siebe Plc 24p to 1,118-1/2p.
Carlton Communications Plc rose 9p to 497p, Pearson Plc 24-1/2p to 764-1/2p and Reuters Holdings Plc put on 19p to 682p.
"It's a way to play the currency markets in equities," said NatWest Securities' analyst Neill Junor, referring to Reuters.
"People are looking at it as a currency surrogate," he said.
